name: Economics: Kidney exchange clearing with two- and three-way cycles
description: Choose vertex-disjoint two- and three-way exchange cycles in eight public kidney-exchange pools of 256 and 512 incompatible patient-donor pairs to maximize the number of transplants. The evaluator verifies every donor-patient compatibility on the chosen cycles and compares the transplant count with the proven optimum.

sources.locator: Roth, Sonmez and Unver (2007): kidney exchange with two- and three-way exchanges among incompatible patient-donor pairs and the gains from three-way cycles.
Abraham, Blum and Sandholm (2007): the clearing problem with a cycle-length cap, its NP-hardness for caps of 3 or more, and exact integer-programming clearing for nationwide pools.
Saidman et al. (2006): the pool generator (blood types, PRA levels, spousal donors) used for the PrefLib instances.
PrefLib dataset 00036 (kidney), pinned commit: pools 00036-00000151..154 (256 pairs) and 00036-00000191..194 (512 pairs), no altruists.

requirements.datasets: Eight PrefLib kidney pools (GPL-3.0) fetched from a pinned commit by scripts/prepare_finance.py and verified by SHA-256; not redistributed.

evaluation.benchmark: Economics: Kidney exchange clearing with two- and three-way cycles
evaluation.paper_metric: Local protocol; see candidate contract and source adaptation notes

execution.interface: select_exchanges(pool) -> list of cycles; each cycle is a list of 2 or 3 distinct pair indices [v1, ..., vk] such that the donor of v1 is compatible with the patient of v2, ..., and the donor of vk with the patient of v1, and no pair appears in two cycles. pool = {'name': str, 'pairs': n (256 or 512), 'edges': (E, 2) int array of compatible (donor_pair, patient_pair), 0-based, 'max_cycle_length': 3, 'time_limit_seconds': 60.0 (advisory)}. Called once for each of eight PrefLib kidney pools (00036-00000151..154 with 256 pairs, 00036-00000191..194 with 512 pairs, no altruists). Score: total transplants (pairs on the chosen cycles) divided by the total proven optimum, 1945 (maximize; 1 is optimal). The whole evaluation must finish within 600 s. The candidate runs in a separate sandboxed process: numpy, scipy, scikit-learn and the other installed packages are importable, while the evaluator's library, its data files, the network and subprocesses are not accessible; one thread and 3 GB of memory. It receives only the arguments described here, one call at a time: the arguments of a call are sent after the value of the previous call has been received. Arguments and return values travel as numbers, strings, lists, dicts with string keys and numeric numpy arrays, so a tuple arrives as a list

limitations: The pools are synthetic (Saidman et al. generator, donated to PrefLib by John Dickerson), not registry data; PrefLib removed other faulty kidney instances in September 2026 and only pools without altruists are used here.

Static, single-period clearing that maximizes the number of transplants: no altruist-initiated chains, no crossmatch-failure probabilities, no patient priorities or weights and no dynamic arrivals, all of which matter in practice.

Every pool's optimum is known, so a score of 1 reproduces the integer-programming solution; the 600 s limit makes the task about fast clearing on the larger pools, and time-limited candidates can depend on hardware.

The candidate runs in a sandboxed child process that never receives later data, realised outcomes or reference solutions, and no statement of the candidate is executed in the evaluator's process; outside macOS (kernel sandbox) deliberately hostile native code could bypass the file policy.

state_of_the_art.statement: The optimum of every pool is proven by an exact integer program over all 2- and 3-cycles (optimal transplants 166, 175, 158, 145, 351, 337, 300 and 313; 1945 in total), so the best possible score is 1. The greedy two-cycle seed scores 0.861.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Organize exchanges among incompatible patient-donor pairs so that as many patients as possible receive a compatible living-donor kidney.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Kidney exchange increases the number of living-donor transplants for patients with willing but incompatible donors; clearing pools optimally under operational cycle limits is NP-hard and directly affects how many patients are transplanted.
